Following the adoption of the European Commission’s proposals for regulations on the Digital 
Services Act (DSA) and the Digital Markets Act (DMA) on 15 December 2020, COMECE 
Secretariat would like to submit its feedback to the European Commission.  
 
 
COMECE Secretariat welcomes: 
 
1. Protecting smaller actors such as SMEs to support fair competition and innovation: A 
central challenge of the DSA/DMA is to preserve innovation and competition for a proper 
functioning EU internal digital market, while protecting smaller actors such as SMEs.

2. Paragraph 2 
The Proposal obliges the Commission to review whether the conditions for suspension continue 
to be fulfilled year after year. Given the resources such a review process requires on both ends, 
i.e. for the Commission as well as the respective addressees, the validity of such a suspension 
once taken could be extended. In addition, the period available for the investigation should be 
aligned with the timeframe stipulated in para. 1 in order to speed up the review process and 
thus legal certainty for the addressee.

limitations: Reworded origins are Jev's judgement on BM25's shortlist of passages per adopting amendment: a request that shares none of the amendment's rare words is not judged, and adoption itself (amendment to final act) is still traced word for word.
Shared wording is evidence, not proof of authorship: the Council, the trilogues, a common draft or a coalition can explain the same words.
Every holder of a phrase is credited with the whole phrase (no fractional credit); a phrase with several holders is joint. Members are ranked by their rate per amendment tabled.

A Member's political group is their group on the day the amendment was tabled, from Parltrack's dated group spells; a Member with no spell covering that day counts as group unknown, never under a later group.
333 run(s) of 8 or more words were not counted: they hold fewer than 3 of the law's rare words.
655 amendment(s) have no original wording; their whole text was treated as inserted.
